{{Quote|A Jinda's life is fun and games, because work and play are just the same!|Bondo|<ref name="TTJ" />}}
The '''Jindas''' were a bipedal [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] who were herbivorous and could be easily recognized by their characteristic pom-pom tufts of hair and the markings which covered their bodies. Jindas were noted for their energetic nature and desire to entertain others with their natural performing skills which included juggling, [[Magic/Legends|magic]], dancing, [[Music/Legends|music]], and storytelling. However, the species suffered from a poor long-term memory and sense of direction which gave them a reputation for getting lost.

[[Travelling Jindas|One group of Jindas]] departed [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] around 130 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] aboard the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[Free Enterprise]]'', bound for [[Kuna's Eye system/Legends|Kuna's Eye]] in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]]. However, their ship crashed on the [[Endor/Legends|forest moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]], and the survivors found themselves stranded. The tribe established an [[Farm/Legends|agricultural settlement]] under the protection of the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|powerful]] being known as the [[Rock Wizard]] but were exiled when the Rock Wizard mistakenly accused them of attempting to poison him. Cursed by the Rock Wizard to never be able to settle in one place, the Jindas became a nomadic tribe, taking the name "The Travelling Jindas" and wandering the surface of the [[Moon/Legends|moon]], using their skills to entertain its other inhabitants. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the tribe enlisted the help of the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] in making peace with the Rock Wizard and were allowed to return home. However, their fate remained unknown to the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] until they were discovered by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].

==Biology and appearance==
Though some believed Jindas to be distant cousins of the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|164|Jinda}}</ref> they were in fact a non-Endorian [[Species/Legends|species]] and one of many whose members became shipwrecked on the forest [[Moon/Legends|moon]] over [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="CoE" />

[[File:Jindas-CSWE.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Jinda tribe members]]
The Jindas were a bipedal<ref name="TTJ" /> [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species, which varied in size from slender to rotund<ref name="CoE" /> with an average height between that of an adult Ewok and a [[Dulok/Legends|Dulok]].<ref name="TTJ" /> They could be recognized by their characteristic pom-pom tufts of hair, which could be either red<ref name="CoE" /> or brown in color,<ref name="TTJ" /> and their red or black noses. Jindas had two [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], which were mostly white, with a colored iris around the pupil. Iris colors included blue and green.<ref name="CoE" /> Their feet were larger than those of Ewoks<ref name="TTJ" /> and each had three digits, while they had four digits on each hand,<ref name="CoE" /> while Ewoks had only three.<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> They had large mouths filled with blunt, cube-shaped [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]. The teeth marked them as a herbivorous species, and Jindas were known to be fond of eating.<ref name="CoE" />

Jindas' bodies were mostly a pale brown color, but variations in shade made some darker than others. They bore markings that varied in shape and pattern covering the upper body<ref name="TTJ" /> and forming a band around the neck. Although generally red in hue,<ref name="CoE" /> these markings could take on a variety of shades, both lighter and darker than the main body color.<ref name="TTJ" /> The necks had the ability to expand, making them appear larger than they actually were. This ability served two purposes&mdash;as a defensive mechanism when the Jinda was threatened or as a display which was used by [[Gender/Legends|males]] when attempting to impress a female.<ref name="CoE" /> Though they were a land-dwelling species, Jindas were able to swim in [[Water/Legends|water]] and were known to do so recreationally.<ref name="TCotJ" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Remember, you're with the Jindas. No matter what, it'll be a great show.|Bondo|<ref name="TTJ" />}}
Jindas were a genial species who were said to always have a smile for strangers and displayed a high level of energy, regardless of their physical condition. They had an inborn talent for performing and enjoyed using their talents to entertain others. Though they excelled in performing, Jindas were lacking in other abilities, displaying a poor sense of direction and a limited long-term memory.<ref name="CoE" /> This poor memory and sense of direction was notable among the [[Travelling Jindas|Jinda tribe]] living on the forest moon of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]], who were notorious for getting lost. It was said among the native Ewoks that once the Jindas left a village, they would never return.<ref name="TTJ" />

[[File:JindaDancers-TTJ.png|thumb|right|200px|A Jinda dancing troupe]]
Jinda society was based around entertainment; they used their natural performance skills to entertain others<ref name="CoE" /> and made no distinction between work and play. They had a variety of skills including training performing animals, [[Magic/Legends|magic]] acts,<ref name="TTJ" /> juggling,<ref name="CoE" /> and [[Music/Legends|music]], with instruments including [[Jinda wind instrument|wind]], [[Jinda string instrument|string]], and [[Jinda percussion instrument|percussion]].<ref name="CSWE" /> Dancing was another Jinda activity, and female dancers proved popular with males of other species, including Duloks<ref name="TTJ" /> and [[Skandit]]s.<ref name="TCotJ" /> They were very confident in their skills as entertainers and, in the absence of a willing audience, were happy to perform to even the most blasé or unintelligent lifeforms, such as the tree-dwelling [[choreamnos]] [[Goat/Legends|goats]] on Endor.<ref name="TTJ" /> Jindas were also fond of storytelling, though their poor long-term memory gave them a habit of embellishing their tales. In this, their poor memory proved advantageous as the unintended exaggerations tended to make their stories more entertaining for the listeners. However, no matter how much a Jinda might exaggerate, their stories were always based around a central truth.<ref name="CoE" />

As performers, Jindas typically wore colorful stage costumes,<ref name="CoE" /> even as casual attire.<ref name="TCotJ" /> A variety of [[Hat/Legends|hats]] were common among both genders, as was footwear. Males often wore loose fitting garments on the upper body, typically secured by a belt around the waist, while baggy pants or leggings were worn over the legs. Female Jindas also tended to wear pants but wore tighter fitting garments on the upper body which often left the midriff exposed. Veils covering the face and neck beneath the eyes were also popular among females.<ref name="TTJ" />

The Jinda tribe on Endor was initially a [[Farm/Legends|farming]] community. They grew their own vegetables in fields plowed using large beasts of burden<ref name="TCotJ" /> called [[awor]]s<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://maureenkuppe.com/ewokcels/collectibles.htm|text="Other Stuff: Non-Ewok Cartoon items you might want to see"|author=Maureen Kuppe|work=EwokCels.com|archivedate=20160607064439}}</ref> and survived on meals made from the resulting crops. The Jinda love of food was evident in their cuisine, which the [[Rock Wizard]] considered to be the best he had ever tasted.<ref name="TCotJ" /> The tribe later became nomadic, spending their time wandering the vast distances between settlements.<ref name="CoE" /> They traveled aboard the same beasts who had once plowed their fields,<ref name="TCotJ" /> with their performing equipment and dwellings fastened to the beasts' backs. When stopped, the tribe would set up a temporary camp, using tents and portable huts as accommodation while their beasts rested.<ref name="TTJ" /> The Travelling Jindas used their talents to entertain the lifeforms they encountered on their travels,<ref name="CoE" /> moving from town to town and putting on a performance for the inhabitants. In return for the entertainment, the Jindas asked only for one night's hospitality, though they would accept tips in any form. Although their performances were generally well received, some natives of Endor considered them to be freeloaders.<ref name="TTJ" /> They were a peaceful group, having no enemies on Endor, and often acted as neutral parties, carrying messages between the moon's warring inhabitants.<ref name="CoE" /> Though not native to Endor, the group were able to communicate with native species, including the Ewoks and Duloks.<ref name="TTJ" />

==History==
===The Curse of the Jindas===
{{Quote|He cast a spell to keep us on the move. If we ever returned or fell into a groove, the rocks would rise up, like they did today, and chase us all around until we made our way.|Bondo describes the Rock Wizard's curse|<ref name="TCotJ" />}}
[[File:JindaBeast-TCotJ.png|thumb|left|200px|A Jinda beast plows a Jinda farm.]]
Jindas were known to the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] community as early as 130 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Around 130 BBY, several hundred Jinda and [[Tulgah/Legends|Tulgah]] settlers departed [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]], bound for [[Kuna's Eye system/Legends|Kuna's Eye]] in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]] aboard the colony [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[Free Enterprise]]''. The vessel never reached its intended destination, crashing on Endor and stranding both groups on the unfamiliar forest moon. The Jindas adapted quickly, however, and were able to make a new home for themselves.<ref name="CoE" /> They established a stable agricultural settlement on Endor near the [[Rock Fortress|fortress]] of the Rock Wizard,<ref name="TCotJ" /> a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] being<ref name="CoE" /> with whom they enjoyed a mutually beneficial relationship; in exchange for the Rock Wizard's protection, the Jindas provided him with their finest cuisine, produced from vegetables grown in their fields. The Jindas were content in their new lives and never ventured far from home.<ref name="TCotJ" />

During one of his meals, the Rock Wizard lost a tooth, causing him considerable pain and leading him to conclude that the Jindas had attempted to poison him. The Rock Wizard chased the Jindas from their home and cast a [[Force power/Legends|spell]] that would cause the rocks to rise up and attack them if they ever returned or stayed in one place for too long. Under the leadership of the Jinda [[Bondo]],<ref name="TCotJ" /> the tribe became nomadic, taking the name "The Travelling Jindas" and wandering across Endor, using their talents to entertain the native species and trading with those they encountered, including [[Gupin/Legends|Gupins]] and Duloks. Their poor sense of direction meant that encounters with the more hostile Dulok tribes were infrequent, but also made it difficult for them to find tribes of their favorite audience, the native Ewoks. The Ewoks came to refer to this poor directional sense as "The Curse of the Jindas" and adopted the name "[[Jinda (Ewok)|Jinda]]" as a derogatory term for nomadic members of their own species who shunned their traditional sedentary lifestyle. Ever fond of a good story, Jinda chroniclers would tell the tale of their former life and exile at the hands of the Rock Wizard.<ref name="CoE" />

===Visit to Bright Tree Village===
{{Quote|On behalf of the Ewok village, I'd like to thank you for a magnificent show.''"<br />"''Of course you would. Everybody loves the Jindas. Even the Jindas love the Jindas.|Chirpa and Bondo|<ref name="TTJ" />}}
[[File:TheTravellingJindas-TTF.png|thumb|right|200px|The Travelling Jindas visit Bright Tree Village.]]
In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="EwoksDate">{{EwoksDate|appearance of Jindas|[[The Travelling Jindas]]" and "[[The Curse of the Jindas]]}}</ref> the Travelling Jindas came upon [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]], an Ewok settlement on the forest moon. As they entered the village, Bondo was met by [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]], the Ewok [[Chief/Legends|chieftain]], and offered to put on a show in return for the Ewoks' hospitality for the night. Though some in the village considering the Jindas to be merely freeloaders, Chirpa agreed to let them stay, and that night the Jindas put on a show for the Ewoks featuring performances by the animal trainer [[Chituhr]], the magician [[Trebla]], and a group of [[Jinda Dancers|female dancers]]. The show was well received by the Ewoks, and Chief Chirpa thanked Bondo as the Jindas prepared to leave the following morning. One Ewok, however, was particularly inspired&mdash;the young Ewok [[Musician/Legends|musician]] [[Latara/Legends|Latara]] decided to leave with the Jinda tribe in order to learn from the tribe and sharpen her own skills. Only after leaving Bright Tree Village did the Jindas discover that Latara had stowed away in their equipment. Nevertheless, the tribe welcomed her into their number, and Bondo soon put her to work washing their performing costumes.<ref name="TTJ" />

The tribe continued on their way, unaware that Latara's presence had attracted pursuers&mdash;the Ewok [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] [[Logray/Legends|Logray]] had dispatched [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Wystri Warrick]], [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka]], [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]], and [[Paploo/Legends|Paploo]] to retrieve the runaway Ewok, while a pair of Duloks sought to capture her to present to their leader, [[King/Legends|King]] [[Gorneesh/Legends|Gorneesh]]. The following night, the Travelling Jindas stopped in a clearing in the forest and decided to perform for a group of choreamnos. Latara was enlisted for her first performance, as the assistant in Trebla's magic act. It wasn't long before Latara realized that Jinda life was not as she had imagined and asked Bondo to take her home, but by this point the Jindas were already lost and had no idea how to find Bright Tree Village. The other Ewoks soon caught up with the Jinda tribe, but Latara was already gone&mdash;kidnapped by the Duloks when she ventured away from the Jinda camp.<ref name="TTJ" />

Bondo agreed to help the Ewoks rescue their friend. With the Ewoks disguised as Jindas, the Travelling Jindas headed for the [[Dulok Swamp|swamp]] where King [[Gorneesh's tribe]] resided and offered to perform for the Duloks in exchange for camping in the swamp that night. During the show, Bondo spotted the captive Latara among the audience and selected her to assist Trebla. Gorneesh agreed to allow it, unaware that the Jindas were planning an illusion that would allow Latara to flee with the other Ewoks, who were waiting atop the stage. However, when Paploo fell from the stage, the Duloks realized the deception and gave chase. Bondo turned the tribe's awors on the advancing Duloks, giving the Ewoks time to escape, before he and the other Jindas packed up their equipment and made a discreet exit.<ref name="TTJ" />

===Return home===
{{Quote|Since I am no longer in pain, the curse is off.''"<br />"''You mean&hellip;''"<br />"''Yes, the Jindas may return to the life they once loved beneath my fortress.|The Rock Wizard and Bondo|<ref name="TCotJ" />}}
[[File:RevengeOfTheRocks-TCotJ.png|thumb|left|200px|The Jinda curse strikes.]]
Later that year, the Travelling Jindas stopped to relax near a waterfall on the forest moon. Despite warnings from Trebla that staying too long would incur the wrath of the Rock Wizard, Bondo and the other Jindas were enjoying their relaxation and were reluctant to move on. As Trebla had feared, after several days near the waterfall, the boulders began to rise from the ground and attack the tribe. Bondo quickly had the tribe pack up their belongings, and they moved on once more, soon coming across a nearby Skandit settlement, where they offered to perform in return for hospitality. The Skandits agreed, but as the Jindas unpacked, Bondo heard the sound of a [[Flute/Legends|flute]] coming from the village; following the sound, Bondo discovered that Latara and several other Ewoks had been captured by the Skandits and were being held [[Prison/Legends|prisoner]]. That night, as the Jindas performed for the Skandit tribe, Trebla and a pair of Jinda dancers incapacitated the Skandits guarding the Ewoks and released them. Providing the Ewoks with a Jinda stage costume designed for several beings as a disguise, Trebla instructed them to flee to safety. The Ewoks, however, took a wrong turn and found themselves on the Jinda stage during the show. When the Skandits realized that the Ewoks were inside, they chased the escapees, but the Jindas quickly loaded their equipment and carried the Ewoks to safety aboard their beasts.<ref name="TCotJ" />

The Ewoks led the Jindas back to Bright Tree Village, where Chief Chirpa thanked the tribe for returning their missing youngsters. Moments later, several floating boulders emerged from the forest and attacked the Jindas. Chirpa offered the Jindas the sanctuary of his village as thanks for their assistance, and both tribes retreated to the trees. Once safely out of reach of the menacing boulders, Bondo explained about the curse to the Ewoks, who offered to help the Jindas free themselves and return home. Logray and his assistant Teebo called upon the [[The Force/Legends|power]] of the [[Light Spirit]] to draw several forest creatures to the village. The animals tethered the boulders to the ground with long lengths of rope, allowing the Jindas to safely return to the ground. However, this only prompted the ire of the Rock Wizard, who came to confront the Jindas and the Ewoks in person. The Rock Wizard attacked both groups until he noticed that his tooth was being used as a necklace by the Ewok Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka. When she explained that they had purchased it from a [[Mooth|trader]], the Rock Wizard realized that the Jindas had not been responsible for his pain. Taking the tooth back, he called off the curse and allowed the tribe to return to their home.<ref name="TCotJ" />

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] destroyed the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], a [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] constructed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of Endor.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Alliance [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] discovered the Travelling Jindas, along with the flourishing Tulgah population, on the forest moon, and the galaxy finally learned the fate of the ''Free Enterprise''.<ref name="CoE" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Jinda.png|thumb|right|150px|An Ewok "Jinda" from ''Star Wars Galaxies'']]
Jindas were created for "[[The Travelling Jindas]]," the fifth episode of the [[Ewoks: Season One|first season]] of the [[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']] animated television series, written by [[Bob Carrau]] and first broadcast on [[October 5]], [[1985]]. Carrau later reused the species in the show's seventh episode, "[[The Curse of the Jindas]]."<ref name="Insider27">{{InsiderCite|27|A Star Wars CELibration|A ''Star Wars'' CELibration}}</ref> In [[2004]], "The Travelling Jindas" was compiled with three other episodes into the feature-length [[Wikipedia:DVD|DVD]] film ''[[Tales from the Endor Woods]]''.<ref name="TftEW">''[[Tales from the Endor Woods]]''</ref>

Early sources to reference the Jindas, including the [[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded|second]] and [[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded|third editions]] of ''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]'' and the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', described them as a tribe of Ewoks,<ref name="AGttSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref><ref name="AGttSWU3">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref><ref name="SWE-Chituhr">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref><ref name="SWE-Jindas">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> and the nomadic Jindas that appeared in the [[2003]] [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|MMORPG]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' were depicted as visually similar to Ewoks.<ref name="Galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> In [[2001]], authors [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Robin Pronovost]] wrote an article entitled ''[[Castaways of Endor]]'' for the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine, which included information and [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] stats for several species from ''Star Wars: Ewoks'',<ref name="CoE" /><ref name="DW blog 120">{{Blog|danwallace|120|'Castaways of Endor,' New Article on StarWars.com}}</ref> including a section on Jindas written by Pronovost.<ref name="JCF1">{{JCFCite|url=posts/29533288|board=Literature|thread=Castaways of Endor sees the light of day|user=[[Daniel Wallace|Dan_Wallace]]|date=2008-12-02|time=10:17 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140424052520/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/castaways-of-endor-sees-the-light-of-day.29530570#post-29533288}}</ref> During the course of writing the article, Pronovost discovered that the ''Star Wars Encyclopedia'' had described the Jinda leader Bondo as an Ewok. Noting the numerous visual discrepancies between the depiction of Jindas and Ewoks in the original cartoons,<ref name="JCF2">{{JCFCite|url=posts/29533637|board=Literature|thread=Castaways of Endor sees the light of day|user=[[Daniel Wallace|Dan_Wallace]]|date=2008-12-02|time=12:06 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140424052520/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/castaways-of-endor-sees-the-light-of-day.29530570#post-29533637}}</ref> the two ultimately established that the Jindas from ''Star Wars: Ewoks'' were just one tribe from a non-Endorian species which had become stranded on the planet.<ref name="CoE" /> However, ''Star Wars Gamer'' was canceled before the article could be published, and it was not until [[2008]] that the article was finally released through [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]].<ref name="DW blog 120" /> By this time, the Ewok-like Jindas had been included in ''Star Wars Galaxies'', and the term "Jinda" was [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] to have been adopted by the Ewoks for nomadic members of their own species.<ref name="JCF2" />

The roleplaying elements of ''Castaways of Endor'' were ultimately excluded from the final article, but Wallace later made them available through his website. This material includes roleplaying stats for a "Jinda Commoner," revealing an ability to speak the "Old Jinda" language as well as [[Ewokese/Legends|Ewokese]] and extending their habit of getting lost to their [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] abilities. Two adventure ideas involving the Jindas are also included&mdash;one in which the players encounter a Jinda pilot who miscalculates a [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump, leading them into danger in an uncivilized region of the galaxy, and one in which the players discover that a group of Duloks have taken Jindas, Ewoks, Gupins, and [[Wistie/Legends|Wisties]] captive to be sold into [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]].<ref name="COE cuts">{{WebCite|url=https://sites.google.com/site/danwall88/%22castawaysofendor%22:gamingstats|text="Castaways of Endor": Cut gaming stats|author=[[Daniel Wallace]]|archivedate=20150922060300}}</ref>

The [[1997]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement ''[[Lords of the Expanse]]'' included a [[Jinda system/Legends|Jinda system]] located in the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]].<ref name="LotE">''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''</ref> The Jinda [[Star system/Legends|system]] has since been listed in the appendix to [[2009]]'s ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> ''Lords of the Expanse'' predates the Jindas being established as a non-Endorian species in ''Castaways of Endor'', and whether the Jinda system is intended to be their home system is unclear.<ref name="CoE" /><ref name="LotE" />
